sql:
SELECT z.LocationID, z.Borough, z.Zone, COUNT(t.PULocationID) AS cash_trips
FROM ops.zones z
LEFT JOIN lake.trips t ON t.PULocationID = z.LocationID AND t.payment_type = 2
GROUP BY z.LocationID, z.Borough, z.Zone
ORDER BY z.LocationID

diagnosis.bottleneck: The query scans the entire trips table (495833 rows) to filter for payment_type=2, then hash-joins the 99k qualifying rows to the 265-row zones table, and finally hash-groups the 99k joined rows down to 265 groups. The dominant cost is the full table scan of trips and the subsequent join/aggregation on the 99k-row intermediate result.

hypotheses.claim: A filter on the joined side sits in the ON clause of a LEFT JOIN; the join dominates the cost. (matched: left join lake.trips t on … and t.payment_type = 2)

The hash join builds a hash table on the 265-row zones table and probes with 99167 trips rows; the CAST(PULocationID AS BIGINT) in the join condition adds per-row CPU overhead and may prevent vectorized join execution.

The hash group by processes 99167 rows to produce 265 groups; pre-aggregating trips by PULocationID (with payment_type=2) before the join would reduce the join probe side to at most 243 distinct keys, cutting both join and aggregation work.
